A tutor has recorded the marks (out of 50) for all students in her four classes for an assignment.
All classes have the same number of students.

The corresponding histograms are shown in
Fig.&nbsp;\@ref(fig:VariationHistograms).

1. In which class would the median be the *largest*?  Why?
2. In which class would the median be the *smallest*?  Why?
3. In which class would the standard deviation be the *largest*?  Why?
4. In which class would the standard deviation be the *smallest*?  Why?



```{r VariationHistograms, echo=FALSE, fig.cap="Histogram of marks for four classes", fig.height=6.5, fig.width=4, fig.align="center", out.width="90%"}
set.seed(2015)
# The default: mar=c(5,4,4,2) + 0.1)

rescale <- function(x, lo, hi){
   old <- range(x)
   oldlo <- old[1]
   oldhi <- old[2]
   olddelta <- oldhi - oldlo
   newdelta <-    hi -    lo
   new <- (x - oldlo) * (newdelta/olddelta) + lo

   return(list(y=new))
}



par( mfrow=c(2,2), 
     mar=c(10,4,2,2) + 0.1)
x1 <- rescale(runif(1000, 10, 20), 15, 40)$y
x2 <- rescale(rnorm(1000, mean=15, sd=2), 5, 45)$y
x3 <- rescale(rexp(1000,  rate=20), 16, 48)$y
x4 <- rescale(runif(1000, 7, 23), 40, 50)$y

ylims <- c(0,
           600 )

h1 <- hist(
   x1,
   breaks=seq(0,50,by=5),
   main="Class A (30 students)",
   xlim=c(0, 50),
   ylim=ylims,
   axes=FALSE,
   col=plot.colour,
   ylab="No. students",
   xlab="Marks out of 50"
)
axis(side=1, lwd=1)



h2 <- hist(
   x2,
   breaks=seq(0,50,by=5),
   main="Class B (30 students)",
   xlim=c(0, 50),
   ylim=ylims,
   axes=FALSE,
   col=plot.colour,
   ylab="No. students",
   xlab="Marks out of 50"
)
axis(side=1, lwd=1)


h3 <- hist(
   x3,
   breaks=seq(0,50,by=5),
   main="Class C (30 students)",
   xlim=c(0, 50),
   ylim=ylims,
   axes=FALSE,
   col=plot.colour,
   ylab="No. students",
   xlab="Marks out of 50"
)
axis(side=1, lwd=1)



h4 <- hist(
   x4,
   breaks=seq(0,50,by=5),
   main="Class D (30 students)",
   xlim=c(0, 50),
   ylim=ylims,
   axes=FALSE,
   col=plot.colour,
   ylab="No. students",
   xlab="Marks out of 50"
)
axis(side=1, lwd=1)
```
